verdict.rationale: Penpot documents outbound webhooks that fire automatically when events occur, such as a file being created or updated or a comment being added. That is a native event-triggered action: an HTTP call to another application. Any rule logic or resulting automation has to live in the receiving system, since Penpot shows no rule definition of its own. Missing for 10: user-definable rules or conditions, native in-product actions beyond the outbound notification, a documented event catalog and webhook registration details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Outbound webhooks are event calls from Penpot to other applications. They notify that some event occurred, e.g. a file has been created or updated, a comment has been added, etc.
